easy.q: According to Brother Reid, why are you good enough to teach the gospel of Jesus Christ?
options: Because you have studied for many years
Because you can love the Master Teacher
Because you always feel sure of yourself
easy.why: Brother Reid said the answer is yes, not because we know everything or always feel confident, but “Because you can love the Master Teacher!”

easy.q: Where were many of Brother Reid’s earliest Primary classes held in his village in American Samoa?
options: Beneath the shade of a mango tree
On the sand beside the ocean
Inside a large school building
easy.why: He remembered that many of his first Primary classes “were held beneath the shade of a mango tree,” where his teachers knew and loved each child.

easy.q: Who does Brother Reid say were his first gospel teachers?
options: His Primary teachers
His mission leaders
His parents
easy.why: He said, “My first gospel teachers were my parents.” Their home in the village of Leone was his first classroom of gospel learning.

easy.q: In this talk, what did the Savior promise the fishermen in Galilee He would make them become?
options: Captains of many ships
Fishers of men
Keepers of His sheep
easy.why: The Savior said, “Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.” He would make them into who He needed them to be.

easy.q: What “one simple invitation” does Brother Reid give to every gospel teacher?
options: Plan each lesson far ahead of time
Learn every lesson word for word
Love the Lord and love those you teach
easy.why: He taught that the two great commandments become one invitation for teachers: “Love the Lord and love those you teach.”

medium.q: Brother Reid told of a headline saying the new Sunday School leaders included “an NFL Player.” Why did he share it?
options: To show that well-known people draw more interest to a class
To show that news reports often misunderstand Church callings
To show that he too has wondered if the Lord had the right person
To show that scholars are the best prepared to teach the gospel
medium.why: The headline made him laugh, but it did not quiet his feeling: “Lord, I love You, but do You really have the right person?” Many of us ask the same thing.

medium.q: What “beautiful pattern” did Brother Reid notice in how the Savior invited people to teach His gospel?
options: He usually chose those who had the most experience
He often gave them a promise along with the invitation
He first gave them a hard task to prove their faith
He waited until they asked Him for a chance to teach
medium.why: Brother Reid observed that often, as the Savior invited someone to teach, “He also gave them a promise”—and His promise to help us remains the same today.

medium.q: Brother Reid noted that the resurrected Savior invited the people in the Americas to come to Him one by one before He taught His doctrine. What does this show about how He teaches?
options: He wanted smaller groups so His words were easier to hear
He taught only those who had first shown they were ready
He kept His most important teachings for a chosen few
He began with individuals so each could know Him for themselves
medium.why: He did not begin with a sermon to the multitude. “He began by focusing on the individuals,” and only then taught His doctrine and ordinances.

medium.q: According to Brother Reid, what did the love of his Primary teachers help the children do?
options: Feel the Savior’s love and the truth of His gospel
Remember the details of each prepared lesson
Sit quietly through classes held outdoors
Decide to become teachers when they grew up
medium.why: He said, “Their love helped us feel the Savior’s love, and feeling His love helped us feel the truth of His gospel.” That is the pattern of the Master Teacher.

medium.q: Some may ask, “How can I teach everything in 25 minutes?” Brother Reid offered a better question. What change in a teacher’s aim does his question ask for?
options: From teaching the whole class to working with one learner at a time
From preparing each lesson carefully to speaking without a plan
From covering all the material to helping learners connect to the Savior
From teaching gospel doctrine to sharing mostly personal experiences
medium.why: His better question was, “How can I help those I teach connect to the Savior sooner?” The aim shifts from getting through everything to bringing people to Him.

hard.q: According to Brother Reid, what was the Savior’s first lesson to His disciples about?
options: Teaching—how to share His message clearly
Discipleship—who they were to become
Courage—how to face those who opposed them
Scripture—what the prophets had written of Him
hard.why: Before He taught them where to go and what to teach, He taught them who to become. “His first lesson was not about teaching—it was about discipleship.”

hard.q: What did Brother Reid and his wife learn in the Australia Sydney Mission was the surest way to truly love those they taught?
options: Learning about each missionary’s home and culture
Serving beside them long enough to know them well
Remembering how hard their own first days had been
Deepening their love for the One they taught about
hard.why: As their love for the Savior deepened, He taught them “to see the missionaries as He sees them and to love them as He loves them.” Love for Him comes first.

hard.q: Which situation best fits what Brother Reid said it means to have “taught enough”?
options: A teacher reaches the last point in the outline just as time runs out
Class members go home praising how well the teacher spoke
Time runs out mid-lesson, yet members leave feeling closer to the Savior
A teacher fits in every scripture by talking fast and skipping questions
hard.why: His measure is not how much was covered: if class members leave “feeling closer to the Savior than when they came, we have taught enough.”

hard.q: Brother Reid quoted President Oaks that a gospel teacher will never obscure a learner’s view of the Master “by standing in the way.” What did Brother Reid then say is the purpose of every lesson?
options: For people to leave thinking about and loving the Savior
For teachers to say little and let class members lead
For teachers to keep their own experiences out of it
For people to leave able to repeat what was taught
hard.why: He said the purpose is not for people “to leave talking about the teacher. It is for them to leave thinking about and loving the Savior.”

hard.q: Brother Reid said that when Jesus invited the people to return home and ponder, “class” had ended. What did he teach from what the Savior did next?
options: The people needed more doctrine before they could leave
His love for those He taught went on after the lesson
Pondering at home matters more than learning in a group
A lesson should go on until every question is answered
hard.why: “Class” had ended, “but His love for the people had not.” Filled with compassion, He healed their sick, blessed their children, and prayed for them.
